findings.title: Look-ahead make-ready skips missing predecessors so work is marked can_start
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator deploys LookAheadScheduler.analyze_make_ready / generate_daily_plan as the live make-ready gate.
2. Attacker (scheduler/BIM export) imports a look-ahead window that includes successor steel/MEP but omits unfinished predecessors outside the window (or drops them from master_activities).
3. pred_complete uses `for p in act.predecessors if p in self.activities`, so missing IDs are skipped; `all([])` is True.
4. With no open constraints, can_start=True and generate_daily_plan dispatches the crew onto incomplete predecessors.
findings.why_not_blocked: No fail-closed check that every predecessor id exists and is COMPLETE; window filtering silently drops FS links.
findings.poc_idea: Activity A200 predecessors=['A050'] with only A200 imported → can_start True; daily plan includes A200.

findings.title: Resource leveling has no FS links and can start predecessors after successors
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses ResourceOptimizer.level_resources() as the live crew/crane schedule.
2. Foundation (A, float) and steel (B, critical) share a capacity-1 crane and overlap.
3. Leveling only shifts non-critical activities and _find_valid_start only checks resource capacity — Activity has no predecessors field.
4. Result starts A on day 15 while critical B remains on day 5 → steel authorized before foundation finishes.
findings.why_not_blocked: No predecessor/successor model; critical path activities are never shifted so the only resolution is moving the predecessor later.
findings.poc_idea: A ES=0 float, B ES=5 critical, both CRANE:1 → after level_resources starts A=15, B=5.

findings.title: Schedule compression forges achieved_reduction and fast-track duration without CPM
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses crash_schedule / optimize_compression for LD/EOT recovery plans.
2. Parallel critical paths: crashing Path1 days does not shorten the project while Path2 remains.
3. days_achieved increments per crash day; CompressionPlan.achieved_reduction uses that counter, not original−new CPM duration.
4. fast_track_schedule subtracts caller-supplied overlap_days from duration without mutating the network; optimize_compression adds inflated crash+FT into new_project_duration.
findings.why_not_blocked: achieved_reduction is not recomputed from calculate_project_duration(); fast-track never applies overlaps to predecessors.
findings.poc_idea: Two parallel 25d paths crash 10 days → claimed achieved=10, actual duration drop=0. FT overlap 25 → reported duration 25 while A still 20d.

findings.title: Fleet assign_equipment double-books IN_USE and pulls units out of MAINTENANCE
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses assign_equipment as the live dispatch API (get_available_equipment is display-only).
2. Attacker assigns the same crane to SiteA then SiteB without return_equipment.
3. Both Assignment records stick; status stays IN_USE.
4. Same call also succeeds when status was MAINTENANCE/REPAIR, forcing IN_USE and authorizing overloaded/unsafe equipment on a second site.
findings.why_not_blocked: assign_equipment only checks equip_id existence; never requires AVAILABLE or clear prior open assignments.
findings.poc_idea: assign SiteA then SiteB → 2 assignments; set MAINTENANCE then assign SiteC → succeeds, status IN_USE.

findings.title: Labor assign_worker only warns on conflicts then keeps both assignments on the roster
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses assign_worker + get_daily_roster for crew dispatch.
2. Attacker (or agent) assigns the same ironworker to overlapping ZoneA and ZoneB activities.
3. check_conflicts finds the overlap but only prints a Warning; assignment is still appended.
4. Daily roster lists both activities → one zone is staffed on paper while the certified worker cannot be in two places (unsafe/under-crewed work authorized).
findings.why_not_blocked: Conflict detection is advisory; no return None / raise on overlap; no check for ON_LEAVE/SICK/TERMINATED either.
findings.poc_idea: Two overlapping assign_worker calls → len(assignments)==2 and get_daily_roster has both rows.

findings.title: Telematics CRITICAL faults never flip status to FAULT so equipment stays dispatchable
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses get_current_status / generate_report as the go/no-go for crane dispatch.
2. ingest_reading with coolant_temp=120 creates COOLANT_TEMP_HIGH CRITICAL via _check_diagnostics.
3. operating_status is still derived only from engine_rpm/load (OPERATING).
4. get_current_status returns status='operating' with active_faults>0; fleet report shows operating — crane stays authorized.
findings.why_not_blocked: OperatingStatus.FAULT and FaultSeverity.SHUTDOWN exist but ingest_reading never sets them; status path ignores active faults.
findings.poc_idea: coolant_temp=120, rpm=1500 → CRITICAL fault present and status=='operating'.

findings.title: Punch verify_item accepts OPEN CRITICAL items without completion or rework gate
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator uses PunchListManager for final/occupancy punch closeout.
2. Attacker creates a CRITICAL life-safety punch (e.g. missing fire damper) and calls verify_item(..., accepted=True) while status is still OPEN.
3. No requirement for READY_FOR_VERIFICATION, photo_after, or prior mark_complete.
4. Item becomes ACCEPTED; get_statistics completion_rate=100% → forged closeout authorizing occupancy with open life-safety defects.
findings.why_not_blocked: verify_item has no status precondition and does not inspect priority/trade before ACCEPTED.
findings.poc_idea: add CRITICAL fire-protection item → verify_item accept from OPEN → ACCEPTED and completion_rate 100.
